land.text: the Khitan homeland south of the Xar Moron and east of the Laoha river, under the Yaonian clan until Abaoji's accession

predecessors.note: Abaoji 'became khagan of the Khitans on 27 February 907' and 'founded the Liao dynasty in 907' (Khitan people page); the Liao page lists the dynasty from 916 (emperor) but calls the Great Khitan State 'founded in 907 by Abaoji'. Cliopatria's Liao row starts in 911.

land.text: Manchuria, the Liaoxi and eastern Inner Mongolia, the Liao circuits taken 1115-1125

successors.note: 'Destruction of the Liao dynasty: 26 March 1125' (Jin page infobox); Tianzuo captured in early 1125.

land.text: the successor state established by Yelu Dashi in the Western Regions, which 'in 1124 officially adopted the dynastic name Great Liao'

successors.note: Western Liao (Qara Khitai), 1124; the Sixteen Prefectures also passed briefly to the Song in 1123 (Sixteen Prefectures page).

capitals.name: Khitan royal camp (ordo) on the Xar Moron
capitals.note: Approximate: the court was itinerant until the walled city of 918; the pages give no earlier seat.

capitals.name: Shangjing (Linhuang)
capitals.note: 'In 918, Abaoji had a new walled city built' (Taizu page); the Liao page: the court moved to Shangjing two years after 916. Four more capitals followed: Nanjing (Beijing, after 938), Zhongjing (walls built 1018-1020), Xijing (Datong, formally 1044) and Dongjing (Liaoyang).

rulers.name: Taizu (Yelu Abaoji)
rulers.note: Table: 916-926 as emperor; khagan from 27 February 907 (Taizu page); died 6 September 926.

rulers.name: Tianzuo (Yelu Yanxi)
rulers.note: Captured by the Jin in early 1125; page gives no temple name.

keyframe_review.note: The 266 thousand km2 Khitan core (111-125 E, 40-44.8 N) is plausible for the Khitan homeland 'south of the Xar Moron River and east of the Laoha'. The state begins on 27 February 907 (khagan) and the shape is used from 907. No infobox area exists before 947.

426 thousand km2: the step adds 199 thousand km2 of Inner Mongolia west of the core (107-118 E). The Khitan page only says 'all the Kumo Xi, Shiwei, Tatars, western Turks and Jurchens had been defeated' by Abaoji's time and the Taizu page has deep raids into Hebei in 922 and 923; no page dates the annexation. Unverified: page silent on the year.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 926-937; Balhae land drawn as Dongdan vassal 926-935

keyframe_review.note: 1.76 M km2: adds Balhae (fell 'in 926' when the Khitans besieged Shangjing and forced its surrender) and the Mongolian steppe to 99.9 E. The shape holds 926-937; the Balhae land was the autonomous Dongdan kingdom under Yelu Bei (independence ended in 929 with the relocation of its people) and was 'absorbed into the Liao in 936'. Steppe expansion 924-926 is undated on the pages opened. fx-24 (1 Nov 2026, F253): 'to' 937 added so that this shape, not the 936 shape with the Sixteen Prefectures, is the one alive in 936-937 (the correction text already said valid 926-937).

1.92 M km2: adds the Sixteen Prefectures (111-120 E, 38.5-40 N). Shi Jingtang promised them in 936 (Five Dynasties page) but 'in 938, the puppet emperor of Later Jin transferred the Sixteen Prefectures over to the Khitans' (Liao page); the shape belongs from 938. Infobox area 947: 2.6 M km2 against 1.92 M km2 (ratio 0.74): inside the factor of two. fx-24 (1 Nov 2026, F253): 'from' 938 added; without it the keyframe began with the Cliopatria shape's own start year 936 and claimed the Sixteen Prefectures (870 cells) from the Later Tang, which held them until 937 (later-tang ledger 13-14). Sixteen Prefectures page: 'The Sixteen Prefectures passed into Liao hands in 938'; 'In 938 AD, the prefectures were ceded to the Khitans' (the page also has 937 once).
1.92 M km2, no change: the Song attack of 979 (Gaoliang River) and 986 moved no frontier; the Sixteen Prefectures held until 1123.
No change in area; 983 name change only.

Four cells moved at the Ordos edge (Western Xia appears as a neighbour from 990); the Chanyuan Treaty of January 1005 'finalized' the Song frontier along the Sixteen Prefectures. The Sinuiju disc at the Yalu mouth (10 thousand grid-km2) is inside this shape throughout 990-1039; the ledger records Liao possession only 1014-1031 (Goryeo page, Goryeo-Khitan War page) and the disc is not split out.
Three cells moved on the western edge (97.9 E); the Liao invasions of Western Xia in 1044 and 1048 took no land.

Cliopatria keeps one shape to 1125, but Aguda's Jin took Ningjiangzhou (November 1114) and Huanglong (1115), the Supreme Capital (mid-1120), the Central Capital (winter 1121-22), the Western Capital (spring 1122) and the Southern Capital (winter 1122). The shape holds 1111-1114; new keyframes follow.

correction.text: the 1111 shape without Jilin and Heilongjiang, the first Jin conquests

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Jin takes Ningjiangzhou (November 1114) and Huanglong Prefecture (1115) and proclaims itself. The Jilin and Heilongjiang parts of the Liao shape are the researcher's reading of 'Huanglong' (Nong'an, Jilin).

correction.text: the 1115 shape without the Supreme Capital (Shangjing) district

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'The Jin captured the Supreme Capital in mid-1120' (Linhuang, in the Liao heartland on the Xar Moron).

correction.text: the 1120 shape without the Central (Chifeng), Western (Datong) and Southern (Yanjing) capitals' circuits

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Central Capital falls in the winter of 1121-22, the Western Capital in the spring of 1122 and 'in the winter, Aguda took the Southern Capital'; Tianzuo was captured in early 1125 (infobox 26 March 1125). The page does not date Dongjing (Liaoyang) and the Liaoning part stays in the shape (confidence 2). Valid 1122-1123; the Orkhon Valley leaves it in 1124 (next keyframe).

minus.text: the 1120 shape without the Central (Chifeng), Western (Datong) and Southern (Yanjing) capitals' circuits
the Kedun garrison, 'probably along the Orkhon River in Bulgan Province' (the kara-khitans dossier's founding region)

correction.text: the 1122 shape without the Orkhon Valley, where Yelu Dashi founded the Kara-Khitans in 1124

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 1124 the successor state established by Yelu Dashi in the Western Regions' took the Liao name; the Orkhon Valley (kara-khitans founding region) is split off, the rest of the steppe stays Liao until 26 March 1125. Added after review.

region.text: the Khitan homeland on the Xar Moron and Laoha

ledger.note: 907: Abaoji becomes khagan of the Khitans. 'He became khagan of the Khitans on 27 February 907' (Taizu page); the Liao page: 'In 907, Abaoji demanded that he be made Khagan'; infobox 'Abaoji becomes khagan: 907'.
916: Abaoji takes the title of Celestial Emperor. 'In 916, Abaoji assumed the title of Celestial Emperor'; the Liao page lists the dynasty from 916.
918: the first walled capital. 'In 918, Abaoji had a new walled city built'; the Liao page puts the court at Shangjing two years after 916.

region.text: the Inner Mongolian steppe west of the Khitan core, 107-118 E

ledger.note: 922: the Khitan lands extend west. The year is Cliopatria's step; the page says only that 'all the Kumo Xi, Shiwei, Tatars, western Turks, and Jurchens had been defeated' by Abaoji's time and (Taizu page) that he 'led an army deep into Hebei in 922 and 923'. Tribal lands, so counterpart nobody. Re-opened after review: the Emperor Taizu page dates only the Hebei raids of 922 and 923 and gives no steppe campaign; the step stays Cliopatria's (confidence 1).

region.text: Balhae

ledger.note: 926: the Khitans destroy Balhae. 'In 926, the Khitans laid siege to the Parhae capital Shangjing/Sanggyeong and forced their surrender'; the Taizu page: his campaigns went on 'right up until his death in 926 with the conquest of Balhae' (6 September 926).

region.text: the Mongolian steppe added in the 926 shape, outside Balhae

ledger.note: 926: the steppe to the Altai edge. The Taizu page says his 'westward expansion reached far onto the Mongolian Plateau' without a date; the year is Cliopatria's step. Re-opened after review: the Emperor Taizu page gives no date for the Mongolian Plateau expedition; the step stays Cliopatria's (confidence 1).

region.text: Balhae's land as the autonomous kingdom of Dongdan

ledger.note: 926: the Dongdan kingdom under Yelu Bei. 'In Parhae's place, the Khitans established the autonomous kingdom of Dongdan', ruled by the Liao crown prince Yelu Bei.

region.text: the Dongdan kingdom

ledger.note: 936: Dongdan is absorbed into the Liao. 'Its independence ended in 929 when a new Liao ruler ordered the relocation of its population' and 'it was soon absorbed into the Liao in 936' (Balhae page); the Dongdan dossier uses 936.

region.text: the Later Jin realm as it stood under Liao suzerainty: the Cliopatria 936 shape (from January 937 the Later Tang heartland without Sichuan; the Sixteen Prefectures until 938)

ledger.note: 28 November 936: the Later Jin is founded as a Liao client. The page's infobox: 'Shi Jingtang proclaimed Emperor by Liao: 28 November, 936'; 'It was founded by Shi Jingtang (Emperor Gaozu) with aid from the Liao dynasty, which assumed suzerainty over the Later Jin' (re-opened). The Sixteen Prefectures are inside the Liao from 938 (gain below) and not in the Cliopatria Later Jin shape. Added after review: the vassal event belongs to the suzerain; the later-jin dossier carries the same pair with this slug as counterpart.

region.text: the Sixteen Prefectures

ledger.note: 938: the Sixteen Prefectures pass to the Khitans. 'In 938, the puppet emperor of Later Jin transferred the Sixteen Prefectures over to the Khitans'; Shi Jingtang was invested by the Khitans on 28 November 936 and 'promised annual tribute and the Sixteen Prefectures' (Five Dynasties page, 936). Cliopatria draws them from 936.

region.text: the Later Jin realm as it stood under Liao suzerainty: the Cliopatria 936 shape (from January 937 the Later Tang heartland without Sichuan; the Sixteen Prefectures until 938)

ledger.note: 942: Shi Chonggui breaks the subordination. After Shi Jingtang's death in 942 he 'wrote a letter (indicating equal status and not subservience) in which he referred to himself as "grandson"'; the Later Jin page: 'his nephew, adopted son and successor Shi Chonggui defied the Liao' (re-opened). Neither page dates the letter within 942, so the year is the accession's (confidence 2). Added after review.

region.text: the Hebei plain up to the Yedu region

ledger.note: 944: the Liao invade the Hebei plain. 'In early 944, Emperor Taizong led a major invasion into Later Jin territory, and quickly reached Yedu'; 'In late 944, Liao again made a major invasion, advancing all the way to the Yedu region, but soon withdrew again' (re-opened). Zone as in later-jin. Added after review.

region.text: the Hebei plain up to Kaifeng

ledger.note: 11 January 947: Kaifeng falls to the Liao. 'Shi Chonggui surrendered the imperial seals that day to Emperor Taizong of Liao' (footnote: 11 January 947); 'Emperor Taizong subsequently entered Daliang' (re-opened). Replaces the occupation of a Kaifeng disc after review: the Later Jin ends here.

region.text: the Later Jin realm, annexed by the Liao in January 947

ledger.note: January 947: the Liao annex the Later Jin realm. 'the Liao invaded in 946 and in 947, annihilated the Later Jin and annexed its former territories' (re-opened; the Shi Chonggui page: seals surrendered 11 January 947). The Sixteen Prefectures were already Liao land from 938. Replaces the Kaifeng occupation after review; the later-jin dossier records the matching loss.
947: the dynasty takes the name Great Liao. 'Taizong formally adopted a dynastic name, the Great Liao' after the victory (early 947); the page also says 'in 938 or 947'.

region.text: the Later Jin realm minus the Sixteen Prefectures

ledger.note: 947: the Liao lose the Central Plain to the Later Han. The Khitans 'retreated from them early in the next year' and Liu Zhiyuan 'entered the imperial capital in 947 and proclaimed the advent of the Later Han' (re-opened); the Later Han held the Later Jin realm without the Sixteen Prefectures (later-han dossier, which records the matching gain). The page gives no month. Replaces the occupation end after review. fx-24 (1 Nov 2026, conflict F089): counterpart changed from later-han to nobody. The compiler skips a loss whose counterpart carries the matching gain, and later-han's gain (947, no month) runs before this dossier's January 947 annexation of the Later Jin realm, so it found only nobody's land and moved nothing: the Liao kept the realm and in 951 still held 93% of later-zhou_951. Freed to nobody here, the realm is taken by later-han's own 947 keyframe and found, and later-han loses it to later-zhou in 951. Later Han page: 'Established in Taiyuan: March 10, 947'; 'The Later Han held essentially the same territory as the Later Jin'; Liao Taizong 'died of an illness in May 947' on the return march; 'Liu Zhiyuan established his capital at Bian, present day Kaifeng'.

region.text: the Song-Liao frontier round Youzhou and the Baigou line

ledger.note: 979: the Song attack Youzhou and lose at the Gaoliang River. The Song army 'lost a crucial pitched battle on the Gaoliang River' (the page's summer of 979); the Song invasion of 986 was 'defeated'; the Liao struck toward Kaifeng in 1004.
983: the name goes back to Great Khitan. 'The name was changed back to Great Khitan in 983.'

region.text: the Song-Liao frontier

ledger.note: 1005: the Chanyuan Treaty. 'In January 1005, the two sides signed the Chanyuan Treaty': the Song pay yearly tribute in silk and silver, the emperors are equals and 'the disputed border would be finalized'.

region.text: Goryeo's north-west frontier and the Yalu

ledger.note: 1010: the Liao invade Goryeo with 400,000 and burn Kaesong. 'The Liao dynasty attacked with 400,000 troops in 1010, claiming to avenge the murdered Mokjong'; invasions also in 993 and 1018, attacks in 1015-1017 were indecisive.

region.text: the Poju (Uiju) region at the mouth of the Yalu

ledger.note: 1014: the Liao take the Poju (Uiju) region. 'The Khitans built a bridge across the Yalu River in 1014 and attacked in 1015, 1016, and 1017'; 'Goryeo lost the Poju (Uiju) region' (Goryeo page, re-opened). The page does not date the loss within 1014-1017; 1014 follows the goryeo dossier, which records the matching loss. Added after review. Cliopatria's Liao shape holds this 10 thousand grid-km2 disc throughout 990-1039, so no keyframe is split for it.

region.text: the Liao-Goryeo frontier

ledger.note: 1022: peace with Goryeo. 'Goryeo adopted the reign title of the Liao in the fourth month of 1022'; the peace was 'formalized in 1022'; the Liao later 'ceded territory around the Yalu to Goryeo' (undated).

region.text: territory around the Yalu

ledger.note: 1031: the Liao cede territory round the Yalu to Goryeo. 'Goryeo broke off relations with Song and the Liao ceded territory around the Yalu to Goryeo' after Wang Heum was invested in 1031 (Goryeo-Khitan War page, re-opened). The region is read as the Poju area of 1014 (goryeo dossier, which records the matching gain). Added after review.
1066: Daozong restores the name Great Liao. 'In 1066, Daozong reintroduced the name Great Liao.'

region.text: eastern and northern Manchuria outside the Liao's land: the Jurchen country of Heilongjiang and Jilin

ledger.note: By the 11th century the Jurchens were Liao vassals: 'By the 11th century, the Jurchens had become vassals of the Khitan rulers of the Liao dynasty' (Jurchen people page; no year given, so 1074, the start of the jurchen-confederation dossier, is used for the pairing). Cliopatria's Liao shape does not include the Jurchen country. Re-opened after review: the Jurchen people page says only 'By the 11th century, the Jurchens had become vassals of the Khitan rulers of the Liao dynasty' and 'The Jurchens switched allegiances between Liao and Goryeo multiple times'; no year, so 1074 stays a bridge (confidence 1).

region.text: eastern and northern Manchuria outside the Liao's land: the Jurchen country of Heilongjiang and Jilin

ledger.note: September 1114: Aguda rebels. 'Starting in 1114, Aguda united the Jurchen tribes under his rule and rebelled against the Liao dynasty'; in September 1114 he rallied 2,500 men at Liushui (near Fuyu, Jilin) and openly rebelled.

region.text: Ningjiangzhou, Huanglong and the Jin heartland

ledger.note: November 1114: the Jurchens win at Chuhedian. Aguda rebelled openly in September 1114; 'his cavalry captured Ningjiangzhou ... and defeated a 7,000-strong Liao army at the Battle of Chuhedian in November' (Wanyan Aguda page, re-opened). The Jin did not exist yet: counterpart changed from great-jin to jurchen-confederation after review (as in that dossier).

region.text: Ningjiangzhou, Huanglong and the Jin heartland

ledger.note: January 1115: the Jurchen confederation becomes the Jin. 'In January 1115, following a series of military successes, Aguda proclaimed himself emperor, established the Jin dynasty' (re-opened); the war goes on with the great-jin counterpart. Added after review.

region.text: Ningjiangzhou, Huanglong and the Jin heartland

ledger.note: January 1115: the war on the Liao continues under the Jin (Wanyan Aguda page); in August 1115 'his army conquered Huanglong Prefecture'. Paired with the end of 1125-03. Added after review.

region.text: Huanglong Prefecture and the country north-east of the Liao heartland

ledger.note: August 1115: Huanglong falls to the Jin. 'In August, his army conquered Huanglong Prefecture' (Wanyan Aguda page; the Jin page: 'late autumn'); Aguda proclaimed the Jin in January 1115 (infobox 28 January). Region is the researcher's reading of Huanglong (Nong'an, Jilin).

region.text: the Supreme Capital (Shangjing) and its district

ledger.note: 1120: the Supreme Capital falls. 'The Jin captured the Supreme Capital in mid-1120.' The Wanyan Aguda page: 'between 1119 and 1122 his army captured all of the Liao dynasty's five capitals'.

region.text: the Central Capital (Zhongjing) district

ledger.note: 1122: the Central Capital falls ('winter 1121-22' on the page; 1122 used).

region.text: the Western Capital (Xijing)

ledger.note: 1122: the Western Capital falls. 'The Jin took the Western Capital in the spring of 1122.'

region.text: the Southern Capital (Yanjing) and its circuit

ledger.note: 1122: the Southern Capital falls. 'In the winter, Aguda took the Southern Capital'; in 1123 the Jin cede most of the Sixteen Prefectures to the Song (Sixteen Prefectures page).

region.text: the Kedun garrison, 'probably along the Orkhon River in Bulgan Province' (the kara-khitans dossier's founding region)

ledger.note: 1124: Yelu Dashi founds the Western Liao. 'In 1124 the successor state established by Yelu Dashi in the Western Regions also officially adopted the dynastic name Great Liao.' Fixed after review: the land is the Orkhon Valley round Kedun, as in the kara-khitans dossier's founding event, not the whole Mongolian Plateau; the rest of the steppe stays in the Liao shape to 1125.

region.text: the whole Jin conquest zone

ledger.note: 26 March 1125: the last Liao emperor is taken. Tianzuo 'was captured in early 1125'; infobox 'Destruction of the Liao dynasty: 26 March 1125'.

minus.text: the last Liao shape: Manchuria, Inner Mongolia and the steppe
the Kedun garrison, 'probably along the Orkhon River in Bulgan Province' (the kara-khitans dossier's founding region)

region.text: the last Liao shape without the Orkhon Valley: Manchuria, Inner Mongolia and the steppe

ledger.note: 26 March 1125: the Liao end. The Jin 'destroyed the Liao in 1125 with the capture of Emperor Tianzuo' (Liao page); the west continued as the Western Liao (Kara-Khitans).

wars.name: Khitan conquest of Balhae
wars.outcome: The Khitans besieged Shangjing (Balhae's capital) and forced its surrender in 926; Dongdan was set up under Yelu Bei and its people were relocated in 929.
wars.note: The Balhae page has Silla allied with the Khitans in 925.

wars.name: Liao intervention in China
wars.outcome: The Khitans backed Shi Jingtang in 936 (Sixteen Prefectures ceded 938) and the Later Jin emperor surrendered to them in January 947; they withdrew.

wars.name: Song-Liao wars
wars.outcome: Liao wins at the Gaoliang River (979) and in 986; Liao advance toward Kaifeng in 1004; the Chanyuan Treaty of January 1005 fixes the border and the Song pay tribute.

wars.name: Goryeo-Khitan War
wars.outcome: Invasions in 993, 1010 (Kaesong burnt) and 1018-1019 (defeat at Gwiju); peace and Goryeo's adoption of the Liao reign title in the fourth month of 1022; the Liao later ceded land around the Yalu.

wars.name: Liao-Xia wars
wars.outcome: Liao invasions of Western Xia in 1044 and 1048 failed to take the capital; peaceful relations were restored by 1053.

wars.name: Liao campaigns against the Ganzhou Uyghurs and the Zubu
wars.outcome: Expeditions in 1008-1010 against the Ganzhou Uyghurs, a failed siege of Ganzhou in 1027, and the defeat of the Zubu tribes after Mogusi's death in 1100 (about two more years).

wars.name: Jin conquest of the Liao
wars.outcome: The Jin took Ningjiangzhou (1114), Huanglong (1115), the five capitals (1120-1122) and the emperor (early 1125); the Song took Yanjing from the Jin in 1123 and lost it in 1125.
wars.note: Dated capital falls from the Jin page.

certainty.note: Steppe and tribal frontiers; the Song frontier is also unfixed before Chanyuan.
Only the Song frontier is sharp ('the disputed border would be finalized' in 1005); the steppe, Xia, Jurchen and Goryeo frontiers stay soft.
The Jin conquest, capital by capital.

notes:
Cliopatria's Liao row begins in 911; the state begins on 27 February 907 (Abaoji khagan) and the dossier carries the 911 shape back to 907. The Khitan tribes before 907 need a dossier (khitan-confederation, written in this batch if the budget allowed; otherwise a gap).

Shape problems: (1) one shape 1111-1125 although the Jin took the Liao capitals between 1114 and 1125 (new keyframes 1115, 1120, 1122); (2) the 936 step is the Sixteen Prefectures, transferred in 938 (Liao page) after the 936 promise; (3) the 922 and 926 steps (Inner Mongolia, the Mongolian steppe) have no dated page, only the fall of Balhae in 926 is dated. The Liao shape includes Jilin, Liaoning and Primorye, and Heilongjiang only to about 46 N; the Jurchen heartland round Harbin lies outside it.

Not settled: the Liao-Xia relation (Li Jiqian 'installed as King of Xia' in 986 in the Liao page, 'accepted the title' in 990 in the Song-Xia wars page) is a tributary relation the pages do not call vassalage, so no vassal event is written; the Jurchens were 'subjects of the Khitan-led Liao' (Wanyan Aguda page) without dates; Goryeo and the Ganzhou Uyghurs were not vassals on the pages; Northern Liao (Xiao Gan/Yelu Chun at Yanjing, 1122-1123) needs a dossier (Dongdan, 926-936, already has one); the page does not date the Liao withdrawal from Kaifeng in 947; Dongjing (Liaoyang) falls to the Jin on no dated page, so the Liaoning part stays in the 1122 keyframe. Names the gazetteer lacks: none (Linhuang is the place 'Shangjing (Liao)').

Fix round after review (2026-10-19): (1) Later Jin client 936-11 to 942, recorded here as the suzerain (vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart later-jin; the later-jin dossier of ea-04 carries the inverted pair, vassal_start with counterpart liao-dynasty, which should be dropped there). (2) 944-947 contest with the Later Jin added; the Kaifeng occupation of 947 is replaced by a gain of the Later Jin realm (matches the later-jin loss) and a loss to the Later Han (matches the later-han gain); the Sixteen Prefectures stay Liao land. (3) Poju/Sinuiju: gain 1014 and loss 1031 with goryeo (the pages do not date the 1014 loss more closely than 1014-1017). (4) The 1124 split is the Orkhon Valley only (kara-khitans founding region), the rest of the steppe stays Liao to 1125 (new keyframe 1124-1125). (5) The 1114-11 contest is with jurchen-confederation (to 1115-01) and then with great-jin from 1115-01. Open: the 922 and 926 steppe gains and the 1074 Jurchen vassal_start stay at confidence 1 (Emperor Taizu and Jurchen people pages re-opened: no date); the Sinuiju disc is in the Cliopatria Liao shape for 990-1039 and is not split out.
